To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) recombinant versions and engineered derivatives of natural proteins are the basis of a successful class of drugs, (ii) novel engineered proteins are entering the pharmaceutical market with a focus on oncology and inflammation, and (iii) the development of protein therapeutics requires the combination of basic research with applied knowledge of protein engineering and protein chemistry, and the close interaction with clinicians.

(i) recombinant protein technology has revolutionised medicine, (ii) the first recombinant proteins were natural proteins with optimised pharmacokinetics, (iii) engineered biologics with novel modes of action have complemented the first generation of biologics, (iv) engineered protein scaffolds are novel biologics with the potential to revolutionize medicine.

the combination of a novel, engineered protein scaffold, with the specific affinity of a single domain antibody (sdAb) for a disease target, and a novel mechanism of action based on the inhibition of the interaction of a protein complex, has the potential to provide an innovative and effective therapy for the treatment of inflammatory and oncological diseases.

the engineering of biologics for therapeutic purposes.
the development of novel biologics and their use as therapeutics in the treatment of human diseases.
the development of novel therapeutic proteins and their application in the treatment of human disease.

recombinant proteins have been a major success story in biopharmaceutical research.
engineered biopharmaceuticals have been successful in the treatment of a wide range of diseases, but that their development is still a long and expensive process.
the use of recombinant proteins has become a routine procedure in the treatment of a broad range of diseases.

the use of recombinant proteins as therapeutic entities is a success story.
the use of recombinant therapeutic proteins is a success story.
we are able to produce recombinant human proteins in a cost-efficient manner.

the development of novel biologics is a highly complex process and that it is essential to consider the entire development process as a whole.
